problems.title: Simplify before substituting
problems.question: Simplify $x(x+2)(x-2)-(x-3)(x^2+3x+9)$, then evaluate it at $x=0.25$.
problems.idea: Use the difference-of-squares and difference-of-cubes identities to cancel the cubic terms.
steps: The first product is $x(x^2-4)=x^3-4x$.
The second product is $x^3-27$.
problems.answer: The simplified expression is $27-4x$; its value is $26$.

problems.title: Three factorisations
problems.question: Factor: (a) $4(a-3)^2-9(a+1)^2$; (b) $(x^2-y^2)-1.5(x-y)$; (c) $x^4+x^3y-xy^3-y^4$.
problems.idea: Look for a difference of squares or a factor shared by a group of terms.
steps: (a) Treat the squares as $[2(a-3)]^2-[3(a+1)]^2$. The factors are $(2a-6-3a-3)(2a-6+3a+3)=(-a-9)(5a-3)$.
(b) First write $x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y)$. Taking out $x-y$ gives $(x-y)(x+y-1.5)$.
(c) Group the first two and last two terms: $x^3(x+y)-y^3(x+y)=(x+y)(x^3-y^3)$.
Factor the difference of cubes to obtain $(x+y)(x-y)(x^2+xy+y^2)$.

problems.title: Compare large products without long multiplication
problems.question: Which is larger in each pair? (a) $856767\cdot856773$ or $856770^2$; (b) $53^2-27^2$ or $77^2-64^2$.
problems.idea: Replace products and differences of squares with simpler expressions.
steps: (a) The two factors are $856770-3$ and $856770+3$, so their product is $856770^2-9$.
Therefore $856770^2$ is larger by $9$.

problems.title: Prove divisibility and compositeness
problems.question: Prove that (a) $2^{23}+2^{20}$ is divisible by $72$; (b) $123^3+2^{18}$ is composite.
problems.idea: A visible integer factorisation proves both claims.
formulas: An integer is composite if it is the product of two integers greater than $1$.
steps: Since $72=9\cdot2^3$, the expression equals $72\cdot2^{17}$. Its quotient by $72$ is an integer.
(b) $2^{18}=(2^6)^3=64^3$. Use the sum-of-cubes identity.
Both factors exceed $1$, so the number is composite.

problems.title: A root common to two equations
problems.question: Find the common real solution of $x(x-2)^2(x^2+1)=0$ and $(x^2-4)(x+1)=0$.
problems.idea: List each equation’s real roots, then find the overlap.
formulas: If a product is zero, at least one factor is zero.
steps: The first equation gives $x=0$ or $x=2$. The factor $x^2+1$ contributes no real root.
The second equation becomes $(x-2)(x+2)(x+1)=0$, so its roots are $2,-2,-1$.
The only number in both lists is $2$.

problems.title: Find a quadratic’s minimum
problems.question: Find the smallest value of $x^2-10x+5$ for real $x$.
problems.idea: Complete the square: a real square cannot be negative.
steps: To complete the square, half of $-10$ is $-5$, whose square is $25$.
Since $(x-5)^2\ge0$, the expression is at least $-20$.
This bound is reached when $x-5=0$, that is, when $x=5$.

problems.title: An integer side of a triangle
problems.question: In triangle $ABC$, $BC=1$ cm and $AC=7$ cm. The length $AB$ is an integer. Find it.
problems.idea: A triangle’s third side is strictly between the difference and sum of the other two sides.
steps: Substitute the known lengths: $|7-1|<AB<7+1$.
Thus $6<AB<8$.
The only integer strictly between $6$ and $8$ is $7$.

problems.title: Internal and external angle bisectors
problems.question: At vertex $C$ of triangle $ABC$, draw the internal and external angle bisectors. The internal bisector makes a $40^\circ$ angle with line $AB$. Find the smaller angle between the other bisector and the extension of $AB$.
problems.idea: The internal and external bisectors at one vertex are perpendicular.
formulas: Adjacent interior and exterior angles add to $180^\circ$.
steps: The angle between the two bisector lines is $90^\circ$.
One bisector makes an acute $40^\circ$ angle with $AB$. A line perpendicular to it makes an acute $90^\circ-40^\circ=50^\circ$ angle with $AB$.
Extending $AB$ keeps the same line, so the requested smaller angle is $50^\circ$.
problems.answer: $50^\circ$ (the supplementary angle at an intersection is $130^\circ$).

problems.title: Recover angles from two altitudes
problems.question: In isosceles triangle $ABC$, $AB=BC$. The altitude lines $AD\perp BC$ and $CE\perp AB$ form an angle of $48^\circ$. Find the triangle’s angles.
problems.idea: Angles between two perpendicular pairs are equal or supplementary; the wording does not name which angle is measured.
formulas: Perpendicular lines to $AB$ and $BC$ form angles $B$ and $180^\circ-B$.
steps: The altitude lines are perpendicular to the equal sides. Their intersection therefore has angles $B$ and $180^\circ-B$.
If the $48^\circ$ angle equals $B$, then $A=C=(180^\circ-48^\circ)/2=66^\circ$.
If $48^\circ=180^\circ-B$, then $B=132^\circ$ and $A=C=24^\circ$.
Both triples satisfy the isosceles angle-sum rule. A diagram or a named angle is needed to choose between them.
problems.note: The source gives no diagram and does not name the angle between the altitudes. If it intends $\angle AMC=48^\circ$, where $M=AD\cap CE$, the intended triple is $(24^\circ,132^\circ,24^\circ)$.

problems.title: Two reflections across a side
problems.question: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle BAC=52^\circ$ and $\angle BCA=44^\circ$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AC$ and $H$ the foot of the altitude from $B$. Extend $BM$ to $P$ so $MP=BM$, and extend $BH$ to $K$ so $HK=BH$. Find $\angle PCK$.
problems.idea: The midpoint construction gives a parallelogram; the altitude construction reflects $B$ across $AC$.
formulas: If a quadrilateral’s diagonals bisect each other, it is a parallelogram.
Reflection in a line preserves angles with that line.
For two rays on the same side of a reference ray, their angle is the difference of their angles with it.
steps: $M$ is the midpoint of both $AC$ and $BP$. Thus quadrilateral $ABCP$ is a parallelogram, and $CP\parallel AB$.
More precisely, the ray $CP$ points in the direction from $B$ to $A$. On the lower side of line $AC$, it makes a $52^\circ$ angle with ray $CA$.
$BH\perp AC$ and $BH=HK$, so $K$ is the reflection of $B$ in line $AC$. Consequently $CK$ makes a $44^\circ$ angle with $CA$, on that same lower side.
Subtract these two angles: $\angle PCK=52^\circ-44^\circ=8^\circ$.
